After reviewing Salivan's post and Jurij's post, I am going to amend my thinking when it comes to drawing zones around fakeouts.

Before I focused on finding the DP to FO and the EG of the DP to FO...while I still think that is correct, I am going to instead start focusing on identifying the swap zones that lead to the fakeout...so I don't misread the DP. Sometimes identifying the decision to engulf is difficult and I am trying to eliminate room for confusion or subjectivity in my future trades. It is the subjectivity (lack of true understanding..."eyeballing it") that gets me in trouble..

There are three important zones involved in a bullish FO: A supply zone (FL that held price), the engulf of this zone (the DP to FO) and the engulf of the DP to FO (this is the origin down).

Nothing has really changed as far as the theory, but making sure I have a supply zone (that is also a FL) prior to the first EG will keep me from getting confused and drawing the wrong DP.

When in doubt on the DP to FO, find the previous true supply/demand/origin, wait for the EG and FTR that forms as a result. This FTR contains the DO to FO.

Ask yourself: "Where was the last FL (opposing) that held price down, prior to the FO"? This is the starting point for the three point process of identifying an origin.

AUD-USD Important Flag Boxes.

I understand the concept of FL Boxes better now (before, I was drawing FL Boxes on areas that were not FL's...)

All FL Boxes hold price (or else they wouldn't be FL Boxes). The trick seems to be understanding which FTR's will bounce price...and trading that bounce. Or, you can wait until a FL has been formed, but the key would be knowing that the FL will bounce price a second time. Not all FL Boxes bounce price more than once before breaking.

Why do some FL Boxes bonce price more than once, and how can we predict these bounces? It must have something to do with order flow

author: hoeschec
text:
More Questions to Ponder:

1. Why does price RT deeply inside a FL Box sometimes (before bouncing) and why does price bounce closer to the start of the FL Box? And how does this fit with the concept of FOF and tricks being played?

2. Is there a connection between tricks (FO's) and the FOF that is created as a result, that could indicate the location of a price bounce within a FL Box?

For example, let's look closer at the FL Box below. As you can see, price bounces many times in this zone. I labeled 6 of the most obvious areas of reaction. We see price react for the first time very deep inside the FL Box.. This RT looks like a QM level as well. I can understand why price bounced here.

Here is where the PA gets tricky, and seems a bit random:

You can see price bouncing from #2 - # 5 at the beginning of the FL Box. Each time price bounces from a different level. Sometimes it bounces deeper, then shallow, then a bit deeper, then a little more shallow etc.... With regard to FOF, why does this happen? How can we possible trade these reactions if they are occurring so randomly? The most interesting bounce is at # 6. How are there still orders left here after # 1 already visited the QM level? How can a trader every be able to predict multiple bounces at or near the same level?

More visits to a level = less orders left behind. The more a level has been tested the more likely it is to fail, right

Is our goal to find the most likely area within the FL Box for price to bounce with the lowest risk and highest return (and ignore the other reactions in the scale?) The deeper we look in the FL Box, the lowest the risk and the highest the return.

Another important Question:

At what point do we ID this as a FL Box? Do we have to wait for the new high @ A-4 to form in order to say this is a valid FL Box that bounced price, or can we go to a lower time frame and verify the big FL Box by watching price engulf, RT, and bounce on a 1-min chart somewhere within the wick of the candle at A-1?

If we have to wait for price to bounce at A-3 or A-4 for confirmation of a FL Box, we wouldn't be able to trade the first deep RT in to the box (the first deep RT would be the first test of price entering the FTR, and until it bounced to make a new high, we wouldn't be able to confirm the FL Box.

I know it may seem like I am over complicating things, but I think these are important questions to understand. This is why it is easier to look at historic charts...when the market is live we have to make decisions based on how price is unfolding. We don't have the benefit of hindsight.

When I practice, I always try to look at the chart as if I didn't know how price will end up reacting. I always pretend I am analyzing a live chart (I cover part of the computer screen). These are the questions that come up

First step is learning how to draw the FL Boxes. That part is relatively easy. The next part is knowing which ones are going to bounce price multiple times. As you can see from the chart below, Box A is important and price bounces many times. Box B and Box C are much smaller FL Boxes that bounce price comparatively fewer times. Then, Box D forms and price bounces many times.

Is there a way to know which Boxes will bounce price more than others? Does it have something with the process of swapping from bear-controlled to bull-controlled?

It seems like Box A (Bear Control) and Box D (Bull Control) contain the most FOF. Box B and Box C look like the swapping process that takes Box A and swaps the power to the Bulls controlling Box D. Is this a pattern that is common on different time scales? If so, is there such a thing as 'major FL Boxes" as opposed to 'transitional FL Boxes"?
